T-003.Title: Seventeen locale families, ten languages, parity test

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: All ten static/locales/*.json gain the titleBar.modeChips namespace with exactly fifteen families (owner amendment 2026-10-27, Standard absorbed Reset): short labels split / source / changes / typewriter / focus (5), the menu row label standard (1), hints standard / split / source / changes / typewriter / focus (6), group headers viewGroup and writingGroup (2), narrowNote (1). Copy is native per language from the spec's English reference meanings; product names and ⌘/⌥ notation stay untranslated; RU respects plural rules where applicable. The .min.json twins are what localeLoader ships, but tools/release-normalize.mjs is release-scoped (it also rewrites CHANGELOG.md and the readme manifests) and must not run mid-change; write the twins with a direct compaction — a node loop over the ten sources writing `JSON.stringify(table)` with no trailing newline — and never hand-edit them. The parity test asserts byte equality: `readFileSync(min, 'utf8') === JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(readFileSync(src, 'utf8')))`. New tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js pins presence and parity of all fifteen families across the ten files (and their min twins) — resolving the design-context ReviewLog (Review 4) carry-forward about the Standard row and Reset-all-modes labels by counting them here.

T-004.Title: modeChips.vue: chips cluster with flag truth

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: New src/renderer/src/components/titleBar/modeChips.vue renders the chips cluster: one document-view chip (icon + short label) and compact icon-only chips for active writing modes. Flag truth: chip = diffMode ? Changes : splitView ? Split : sourceCode ? Source : none — read from the current tab's flags and the global preferences, swapping instantly on tab change (like the save-dot). Standard state renders no wrapper element at all (DOM identical to today); with no document open, no chips render. Icon-only chips carry :aria-label from the short label (the pinned consumer of the typewriter/focus short keys — spec carry-forward resolved); every chip's tooltip is its hint, and the Split tooltip appends narrowNote while the editor container is below MIN_SPLIT_WIDTH. Render size and truncation (discharging the spec R-5 plan-duty and the design-context deferral): chip icons render at the cluster's shipped chrome-icon size — the titlebar-nav-btn family, matching the neighbouring theme button, with the final px confirmed by the T-007 visual pass against that neighbour — and a chip label truncates with an ellipsis if the cluster would otherwise crowd the centred filename, the full label always remaining in the tooltip. Mounted in titleBar/index.vue right cluster left of the theme button on macOS and before the caption cluster on Win/Linux; when C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES later adds its button, chips stay left of it. Log marker [TitleBar][mode-chips][BLOCK_CHIPS_RENDERED view=… writing=… tab=…] fires on state changes. UNIT_CONTRACT-ready MODULE_CONTRACT header; unit tests in tests/renderer/components/titleBar-mode-chips.test.js cover the render matrix (view × writing × standard-empty DOM × no-document), narrow-tooltip, and tab-switch swap; titleBar-deep.test.js gains the mount-order assertions.

The popover menu (same component, the document-info popover patterns and neutral chrome styling) opens on chip click with two groups: DOCUMENT VIEW — Standard / Split View / Source Code / Changes, exclusive, checkmark on the visible-surface winner, each row showing its shortcut where one exists (⌥⌘\, ⌘⌥S, ⌘D) and its hint line; WRITING MODES — Typewriter / Focus toggle rows with hints; no footer (Standard is the full reset: view plus both writing modes off — owner amendment 2026-10-27). Menu actions reuse the five existing renderer command paths (view.split-view, view.source-code-mode, view.diff-mode, view.typewriter-mode, view.focus-mode) — no new ids; view selections normalize per the spec: Standard clears splitView + diffMode + sourceCode; Split sets splitView, clears diffMode, leaves sourceCode; Source sets sourceCode, clears splitView + diffMode; Changes sets diffMode, clears splitView. The menu is live: toggles from any old surface while open update rows and chips immediately; outside click closes, inside interactions never close it. Marker [TitleBar][mode-chips][BLOCK_MENU_ACTION command=… view=…]. Unit tests pin the normalization matrix, live reactivity, and close rules.

The focus test asserts computed numbers: non-active paragraph AND an h1 heading at opacity 0.25, the active paragraph 1, all restored to 1 on toggle-off (activeOpacity/headingOpacity assertions — the probe baseline). The typewriter test asserts the stable-line invariant: the active paragraph's center sits within tolerance (60px) of its post-activation viewport position both immediately after activation and after a cursor move to the next paragraph (probe baseline 477→264→264 on a 732px scroller; STANDAR_Y = 320). A regression row asserts the previously-reproducing unlisten pageerror no longer fires (the T-001 repair), with the reproduction recipe pinned here so it is never lost again: drive a flow whose listener teardown calls the @tauri-apps/api unlisten path — mount then unmount the live viewer (raw listen/unlisten at liveViewer/index.vue) or trigger titleBar's resize-listener cleanup (getCurrentWindow().onResized registration) during content interaction; both are verified triggers, and the useIpcListener composable's own consumers (ipc/runtime/search.ts, watch.ts) are further candidates — assert zero pageerrors; plain content clicks alone do NOT trigger it (probe finding), so the row must use a teardown trigger. Runs after `npm run build` with `CI=1` (the T-001 harness rule).

C-2.Expected: Tab A in split, tab B standard: the view chip appears while A is active and disappears on B, swapping in place like the save-dot; typewriter/focus chips (global preferences) do not move or flicker on tab switch.

C-3.Name: Flag truth beats raw flags
C-3.Expected: diffMode on with a lingering tab.splitView=true (reachable via ⌥⌘\ then ⌘D): the chip shows Changes (diffMode > splitView > sourceCode); a menu view switch normalizes — Standard clears all three, Split leaves sourceCode to its own editable-side rule, Changes clears the stale splitView flag; split+source shows the Split chip with source's mirror behaviour untouched.

C-4.Expected: From Split, menu → Source Code is a single action that flips both flags; menu → Standard is the full reset — every view mode and both writing modes off (owner amendment 2026-10-27); displayed shortcuts match shipped bindings (⌥⌘\, ⌘⌥S, ⌘D; typewriter/focus show none).
